summary.headline: CCL Q4 FY26 revenue rose 46% to INR1,226.39 crore and EBITDA 16% to INR193.76 crore; FY27 guidance is ~15% volume and EBITDA growth.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 turnover grew 46% YoY to INR1,226.39 crore, with EBITDA up 16% to INR193.76 crore and net profit up 12% to INR114.53 crore. Management attributed the top-line surge mainly to green coffee price pass-through under the cost-plus model, with volume growth of about 18-20%. Net debt fell by more than INR750 crore to about INR1,073 crore, and net debt to EBITDA improved to 1.45x from 3.1x. Management guided FY27 volume and EBITDA growth of about 15% each, with no large capex planned for two years.

financial_highlights.change: Down more than INR750 crore YoY

segments.name: India branded (D2C/retail)
segments.commentary: Domestic gross turnover about INR650 crore, of which branded sales about INR440 crore. Management says Continental is the number 3 brand nationally and number 2 in some regions and platforms; online is 20-25% of sales. Branded volume grew 25-30% with 15-20% value growth last year.

segments.name: Branded B2C EBITDA
segments.commentary: Management said B2C EBITDA is around 4-5% and will be held at that level, with surplus reinvested over the next 3-4 years. Quick commerce business is about INR100 crore annually.

segments.name: Percol (UK)
segments.commentary: International brand Percol contributes about INR25-30 crore in the UK this year; management targets about INR100 crore within 2-3 years and is evaluating the US and Vietnam.

segments.name: Freeze-dried
segments.commentary: Freeze-dried utilisation runs above the group average and carries higher margins than spray-dried. Management said a higher freeze-dried mix may not rise further next year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: volume growth around 15% and EBITDA growth in line, around 15%.
Branded business: management is committed to about 25% volume growth, with value growth in the same range; no further GST or coffee-price value tailwind expected.
Working capital and debt: CFO indicated gross debt of about INR1,000-1,200 crore next year; management said closing debt of about INR1,100-1,200 crore is plausible.
Interest cost: CFO estimated FY27 interest of about INR100 crore on roughly INR1,200 crore gross debt at about 7.5%, versus INR130 crore in FY26.
Tax: consolidated average effective tax rate is expected to be closer to 17%.
Maintenance capex of about INR25-35 crore per year; no major capex planned over the next two years.
capex_capacity: Overall utilisation about 65% for FY26 with Q4 at about 70%; management expects about 72-73% in FY27 and about 78-80% by FY28, with 85% possible.
Freeze-dried utilisation runs above the group average.
Management said capacity is adequate for about two years; if freeze-dried demand grows faster, options include a strategic tie-up or capacity purchase rather than a large greenfield plant.
Capacity build-out takes about 1.5-2 years to commission.
Vietnam facility is now operating; interest was capitalised last year until it started.
demand_pricing: Green coffee prices are stable, and management expects softening after the Brazil crop; pricing is cost-plus with back-to-back green coffee buying.
Top-line growth of 46% in Q4 comprised about 18-20% volume growth and about 20-25% from coffee price pass-through.
EBITDA per kg fell sequentially in Q4 on a higher share of lower-margin contracts, but management said annual EBITDA per kg improved YoY.
Small packs are about 20% of the business, up from about 15% a year earlier.
Long-term contracts are increasing now that coffee prices are stable, notably for freeze-dried capacity.

Roughly 70% of exports are FOB; on CIF contracts freight and insurance increases are not fully passed through, and Middle East disruption added logistics and energy cost pressure but no route blockage.
B2C discounts are rising because of heightened competition, with brand equity expected to reduce discounts over time.

qa_highlights.question: What was volume growth and was EBITDA per kg down sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume grew about 18-20% on a four-quarter view and Q4 was similar. Q4 EBITDA per kg dipped on product mix, but FY26 per-kg EBITDA improved YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin contraction due to coffee prices, and what is the coffee outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the EBITDA-to-sales decline is optical because of cost-plus pass-through; per-kg EBITDA is unchanged. Coffee prices may soften, which would lower value growth while volume grows.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 15% EBITDA growth be sustained, and why did FY26 outperform?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is about 15% EBITDA growth in line with volume. FY26 gains from freeze-dried mix and efficiencies are already in the base and are unlikely to repeat.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and capacity for the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: No major capex planned for two years, only maintenance capex of INR25-35 crore. Growth beyond capacity could come from tie-ups or outside capacity purchase.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost not fall with lower debt?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about INR25-30 crore of interest was capitalised last year for Vietnam; borrowing cost is 7-7.5%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the export and freight cost effects?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70% of exports are FOB. CIF contracts absorb freight and insurance increases, which cannot always be passed on; availability has not been affected.

risks_watch: Coffee price softening could compress value growth and lower-margin non-premium customers may enter, pressuring EBITDA per kg.
Concentration of margin gains in FY26 (freeze-dried mix, efficiencies) may not repeat, so FY27 EBITDA growth could fall short of volume growth.
Freight, insurance and energy cost pressures on CIF contracts from the Middle East situation.
Capital allocation is undecided between further debt repayment, acquisitions, dividends and new capacity; management gave no commitment.
Quick commerce and B2C discounts are rising, and B2C EBITDA is being held at 4-5%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and balance sheet, but guarded on specifics: management declined to give utilisation detail by plant, withheld capex and capital allocation commitments, and called several items premature. Management also repeatedly explained quarterly margin swings as mix and optical effects.
key_quotes: And therefore, EBITDA as a percentage top line looks contracted, but it is not because what will happen, the opposite will happen probably going forward when in the base, you have higher green coffee prices and going forward, the green coffee prices could soften.
So that is an assurance we are giving that we will not let capacity come in way of growth.
Yes. Profit of freeze-dried is always higher than spray-dried.
we do back-to-back buying of green coffee, which means that we are guarded against any fluctuations, if at all it happens in the coffee prices.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 volume and EBITDA growth of about 15% each (held), backed by utilisation rising from about 65% to 72-73% and branded volume growth committed at about 25%, but no specific new capacity or orders are quantified and no big capex is planned for two years.
